# EHL Atira Challenge: priority plan

Written 10 Oct 2026, 13:15 UTC, from every page of ehl-challenge.atira.ai, the run brief for `public-1`, the
starter kit and the API spec. Raw copies are in `notes/`.

State of the board at that time: 25 teams, 4 ranked, best quality **21.5 / 100**, three teams at 0. The bar is low
right now. A bid that is signed, on the right tender, with the right materials and quantities, is already first.

---

## 1. The game on one screen

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Job | One tender spread over 4 German websites: tender portal (Vergabeportal), supplier portal with the spec (Lieferantenportal), ERP, webmail (Werkpost). Apply the bid rules, enter one priced bid in the tender portal's configurator, sign it with a TAN from the mail. |
| Who decides | A model must choose where to go, what to search and which documents matter, at run time. Code may help: extract a page the model opened, parse a document it picked, paginate a result set it asked for, calculate, validate, retry, fill forms. |
| Clock | Scored run 20 min. Test run up to 2 h (keep it under 20). Setup (max 5 min) and model warm-up are not counted. |
| Browsers | Up to 4 headful Chromium over CDP (`"browsers": 4` in agent.json). Starting your own browser gets it killed. |
| Models | Free hosted Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (OpenAI API, tools, images, 256k) and Clef (yes/no, choice, score). Own keys allowed as team secrets, through the proxy, metered. |
| Answer | Entered on the website. Exactly one submission, and it ends the run. A run with no answer scores 0. |
| Ranking | Eligible (correct tender reference) → quality 0-100 → cost × time (lower is better). |
| Winners | 1. private dataset run, 2. public leaderboard, 3. elegance of the system. |
| Final run | Your **latest** submission that passed review (not your best), on a private dataset: other software, layout, site names, data, and the facts split differently across the sites. Same jobs, same rules, same answer format. |

## 2. What this means (the rules that decide everything else)

1. **Generalise, don't tune.** The final is on websites nobody has seen. No click paths, no URL paths, no CSS
   selectors tied to the public sites. The agent reads the brief at run time and finds things itself.
2. **Quality first, by far.** Cost × time only breaks ties at equal quality. Never trade points for speed. But the
   20 minutes are hard: a late answer is 0.
3. **The last upload is the one that goes to the final.** Never submit an experiment late in the day. Keep every
   tarball you submit, so you can re-submit a known good one.
4. **Opt in to best of 3** for the final (`atira final --best-of 3`). With the free models it costs nothing and only
   the best attempt counts.
5. **Eligibility is nearly free.** The tender reference is in the brief. The only way to lose it is to bid on a
   look-alike tender or not submit at all.
6. **The submission flow is the gate.** No signed bid means 0. Most teams are stuck there. Build it first.

## 3. Where the 100 points are

Bid case (from the brief and scoring docs):

| Part | Points |
| --- | --- |
| Decision (bid / no_bid) | 5 |
| Tender reference | 5 |
| Discount percent | 5 |
| Total net, to the cent | 5 |
| Arithmetic consistency (total = sum of quantity × unit price) | 5 |
| Withdrawn Q&A quantity check (when present) | 5 |
| Dated metal-index check (when present) | 5 |
| Positions, split evenly | 75 minus the two checks, so about 65 |

Inside the positions block, summed over all positions (assuming the 65-point block):

| Field | Weight | ≈ Points |
| --- | --- | --- |
| material_number | 20 % | 13 |
| quantity | 15 % | 9.75 |
| base_unit_price | 15 % | 9.75 |
| surcharge_per_unit | 10 % | 6.5 |
| packaging_per_unit | 10 % | 6.5 |
| rebate_total (project bonus) | 10 % | 6.5 |
| unit_price (final) | 10 % | 6.5 |
| lead_time_weeks | 10 % | 6.5 |

No-bid case: decision 75, reference 5, no positions 5, total 0 → 15. A wrong bid / no_bid call is the most expensive
mistake in the game. Every field scores on its own, there is no penalty for a wrong value, so **always fill every
field with the best estimate rather than leave it blank.** Money is compared to the cent. Extra or duplicate
positions cost one position's share each.

### The ladder (build in this order)

| Step | What the agent gets right | Adds | Running total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | Signed bid, right tender, decision, total = sum (code guarantees it) | 15 | 15 |
| B | Material per position + final quantity (incl. withdrawn Q&A, Satz → pieces) | ≈ 28 | ≈ 43 |
| C | Lead time (stock pooling, commitments) + discount (director mail, threshold) | ≈ 11.5 | ≈ 54 |
| D | Base price (valid condition, scale, price unit, FX to EUR) | ≈ 10 | ≈ 64 |
| E | Surcharge (metal index by date window, setup, shared setup pool) | ≈ 11.5 | ≈ 76 |
| F | Packaging + project bonus | ≈ 13 | ≈ 89 |
| G | Final unit price + total (only right when everything else is) | ≈ 11.5 | 100 |

Step B alone beats today's leader. Steps A and B are where to spend the first half of the day.

---

## 4. Priorities, in order

### P0. Setup (first 30 min)

- [ ] Ask the organizers now: submission deadline, when the final run starts, prizes. Read `/announcements`.
- [ ] Team on the site (up to 5, GitHub invites). `atira login` on each laptop.
- [ ] `claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp` so Claude Code can start test runs, read logs and see screenshots.
- [ ] `atira final --best-of 3` (can be changed until the final starts, do it now so it is never forgotten).
- [ ] GitHub repo created and linked on the team page (organizers ask for it, and elegance is judged on code).
- [ ] Starter kit in `ehl-hackathon/agent/`. **That folder is the package root.** Notes and hand-solved answers stay
      outside it and out of git.
- [ ] `atira models proxy` running in its own terminal; `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` in the dev terminal.

### P1. Hand-solve public-1 once (60-90 min, in parallel with P2 if you have teammates)

- Log into the 4 sites with the scouting logins (`atira scout`) and work out the whole answer by hand, rule by rule.
  Save it as `notes/expected-public-1.json`. Never copy it into `agent/`.
- Why: test runs show points per field but never the right values. A hand answer lets you diff every field in
  seconds on local runs, and it forces you to understand every rule before coding it.
- While doing it, write down **patterns, not values**: where each kind of fact lives, how search works, what breaks
  (popups, timeouts, paging, iframes, ZIPs). These become generic hints in the prompt.

### P2. Thin end-to-end that submits (the gate)

- Generic browser tools (section 5). Login, cookie wall, error retry and re-login are helpers.
- Submitter agent that takes a finished answer JSON plus the brief's submission paragraph and completes the form,
  the TAN and the final dialog. Test it locally with a dummy answer (scouting submissions never count).
- First goal: Step A + B. Then **submit once** to get on the board with an eligible result.

### P3. Climb the ladder (C → G)

- Each step is: a fact the investigators must find + a function in the calculator + a unit test.
- After each step: local run → diff against `expected-public-1.json` → test run in the sandbox for the breakdown.
- Submit a new scored version whenever test runs show a clear gain and it is stable over 2+ runs.

### P4. Robustness for the private dataset (this is what wins)

- Grep the package for any public value: tender reference, company name, VAT id, material numbers, prices, names,
  URL paths, German button labels not in the brief. Zero hits.
- Never assume which site holds which fact. The investigators collect every fact type they see, and a gap check
  sends targeted searches to any site for what is still missing.
- Every UI wording the submitter uses comes from the brief at run time, not from code.
- Run 3-4 test runs of the same package in parallel. Judge by the worst run, not the best.
- Handle no_bid end to end (Verzichtserklärung path) even though public-1 is probably a bid.

### P5. Speed and cost (only once quality is flat)

- Small observations, prompt caching (cached Qwen input is about 10× cheaper), 4 browsers in parallel.
- Clef for cheap yes/no calls (is this the current revision, is this the right mail).
- Only the tie-break uses this, plus a possible small prize for the fastest, cheapest passing run.

---

## 5. Architecture to build

**Model decides, code checks, code computes.** That is robust, easy to defend in review, and reads as elegant.

```
brief (run time) ──► planner: list of facts the rules need
                         │
     ┌──────────────┬────┴─────────┬──────────────┐
     ▼              ▼              ▼              ▼
 tender agent   spec agent     mail agent     erp agent        (one browser each, LLM-driven loops)
 (browser 1)    (browser 2)    (browser 3)    (browser 4)
     └──────────────┴──── evidence ledger ────────┘            (every fact: value, source URL, date, sender, quote)
                         │
                   gap check (model) ──► targeted follow-up searches
                         │
                   rules engine (pure Python, Decimal) ──► answer JSON + self-checks
                         │
                   submitter agent (tender portal + TAN from mail) ──► signed bid
```

### Browser tools (generic, the same on any website)

- `observe()`: compact page text plus numbered interactive elements, tables as rows, content of iframes included.
  Keep it small. Screenshot only when the text is ambiguous (Qwen reads images).
- `click(ref)`, `type(ref, text)`, `select(ref, option)`, `press(key)`, `goto(url)`, `open_tab()`.
- `download_and_read(ref)`: fetch a file the model chose, unzip, extract PDF/HTML/CSV text.
- Auto-helpers the model never has to think about: cookie wall, flaky error page retry, session expired → log in
  again with the run's credentials and return, JS dialogs logged and accepted.
- Never use the browser Back button in the bid form (it clears later steps).

### Agents

- Investigators: one loop per site, with a `record_fact` tool. Each fact carries type, key, value, unit, date with
  timezone, sender, tender reference and a short quote. The model chooses searches and pages.
- ERP agent starts per position once the requirement (after amendments and stroke derivation) and Kataloggruppe are
  known. Positions can be looked up in parallel tabs.
- The model makes the important choices (which tender, which revision is current, which material matches, which mail
  applies). Code then checks them against the rules (dates, exact reference, sender domain, exact attribute match). If
  code disagrees, show the model the conflict and let it decide again.

### Rules engine (pure function, the core of the score)

- `Decimal` everywhere, `ROUND_HALF_UP`. Python `round()` is banker's rounding and will lose cents.
- One function per brief rule, with the rule quoted in a comment, and unit tests with obviously fake numbers.
- Output is always schema-valid, and `total_net` always equals the sum of quantity × unit price.

### Clock guard

- Read `expires_at` from the run. Target: investigation done by about minute 10, submission started by minute 13 at
  the latest, whatever is missing.
- Below about 5 minutes left: stop everything, compute with what you have, submit. A partial bid with the right
  reference beats a perfect bid that is late.
- Measure how long the submission flow takes in test runs and set the cut-off from that number.

### Models

- Start with Qwen for everything: free, unlimited test runs, tiny simulated cost.
- If one step keeps failing (multi-step rule reading, long mails), move only that step to a stronger model with your
  own key as a team secret. Quality beats cost.
- Retry model calls on 5xx and timeouts. A cold model can take minutes, so use long timeouts.
- Hosted limits: 32 Qwen calls and 16 Clef calls in flight per team, across all runs.

---

## 6. Rule traps checklist

Each line is a place where points leak. Tick it when the agent handles it and a test covers it.

**Tender and Q&A**
- [ ] Right tender: exact reference from the brief, look-alike tenders exist.
- [ ] Documents behind "expression of interest" (Teilnahme bekunden): do it early.
- [ ] Iframes, ZIP files, flaky error pages, cookie wall.
- [ ] Quantity = latest dated Q&A change for that position; withdrawn answers (zurückziehen) are ignored, then the
      latest remaining change applies, else the tender quantity.
- [ ] Units: Satz × pieces per set from the **governing** spec revision. Every bid quantity is in pieces.
- [ ] Q&A also assigns: Konditionsgruppe, packaging tariff key, delivery commitment key, shared setup pool members,
      technical amendments. Collect all of them.

**Specification**
- [ ] The portal opens the oldest revision first. Use the one marked current.
- [ ] Nested document viewers and paged requirement tables (read every page).
- [ ] Scoped amendments: only those naming that revision and requirement, only the named attributes, latest dated per
      attribute wins.
- [ ] "nutzbarer Weg": nominal stroke = amended usable stroke + 2 × per-end reserve from the revision-specific
      Technikfreigabe mail.
- [ ] Kataloggruppe per requirement is the ERP search key.

**ERP**
- [ ] SAP-style transaction codes, F4 search popup, short session timeout (auto re-login).
- [ ] Search by Kataloggruppe, narrow to 20 or fewer results (empty or broad searches show nothing).
- [ ] Exact match on bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, certification. Normalise units before comparing.
- [ ] Active only. Blocked materials do not qualify. No match for any position → no_bid. Re-check before declaring
      it (a missed stroke derivation looks exactly like "no match").
- [ ] Price condition valid on the scenario date, both endpoints inclusive.
- [ ] Scale with the highest minimum quantity ≤ final quantity, per position (not per material sum).
- [ ] Price unit (for example per 100 pieces) normalised to per piece.
- [ ] Currency + FX key → Devisenfixing mail → EUR, HALF_UP to cents. That rounded EUR base is used everywhere after.
- [ ] Stock, stock lead time, production lead time, pieces per carton, allocation mass, surcharge mass, ordinary setup.

**Mail**
- [ ] Search is AND: tender reference + topic word. Read inbox **and** archive, all pages.
- [ ] Authorised sender = right local part **and** the bidder's own mailbox domain. Look-alike domains do not count.
- [ ] Latest record dated no later than the scenario date, exact reference. Future-dated and other references never
      apply. A newer record replaces an older one, even if its condition fails.
- [ ] Discount (leitung@): latest exact-reference approval. If it has a minimum order value: undiscounted net value
      (base × quantity, no surcharge, no setup, rounded) ≥ threshold, inclusive. If it fails, 0 %, no fallback.
- [ ] Konditionsregeln (kalkulation@): group → discount on base only / base + mass surcharge / neither. Setup never
      discounted. No group → base only.
- [ ] Preisindizes (kalkulation@): rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last one listed.
- [ ] Technikfreigabe (technik@), Verpackungstarife and Terminfreigabe (logistik@), Devisenfixing and Projektbonus
      (finanzen@), Rüstpools (kalkulation@).
- [ ] TAN: request it only right before signing, use the newest TAN mail, valid 5 min, a new request kills the old.

**Calculation**
- [ ] Shared stock: sum final quantities per material. Stock must cover the whole sum, else every position of that
      material uses production lead time.
- [ ] Delivery commitment: only if its material matches and pooled demand for that material ≤ ceiling (inclusive),
      else the shared-stock rule.
- [ ] Packaging: ceil(pieces / carton size) × tariff, per position, divided by pieces. Never changes quantity. Never
      discounted.
- [ ] Shared setup: one pool fee split by quantity × allocation mass with the cent rule given in the Rüstpools mail,
      added to each member's ordinary setup.
- [ ] surcharge_per_unit = mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + shared setup) / pieces, before discount.
- [ ] Project bonus: marginal bands (like tax brackets) on the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, round once,
      split by largest remainder in cents, ties by ascending position id. rebate_total is per position, not per piece.
      0.00 for non-members.
- [ ] Final unit price = discounted base + discounted mass surcharge + (setup + shared setup + cartons − bonus) /
      pieces, from unrounded parts, rounded HALF_UP once.
- [ ] total_net = Σ quantity × rounded unit price, rounded HALF_UP.
- [ ] Timezones: tender portal shows Europe/Athens, ERP shows UTC, the scenario date is UTC. Convert all to UTC.
- [ ] German numbers: "1.234,56" is 1234.56, and "1.234" is one thousand two hundred thirty-four. Enter prices in
      German format in the form.

## 7. Submission flow (public-1 wording, from the brief)

The private brief will name its own steps, so the submitter follows the brief, not these words.

1. Teilnahme bekunden for the exact tender (also unlocks documents, so do it during investigation).
2. Angebotsabgabe → register the bidder with the company name and USt-IdNr given in the brief.
3. Hauptangebot for bid, Verzichtserklärung for no_bid.
4. Configurator: per position material, quantity, prices, lead time, breakdown fields. "Position auslassen" only for
   positions you really have nothing for.
5. Net unit prices and net total in German format. The gross figure shown includes VAT, ignore it.
6. Acknowledge the tender documents.
7. Request TAN → read the newest TAN in the webmail → enter it within 5 minutes.
8. Read the summary page and compare it with the computed answer before confirming.
9. Confirm "Angebot verbindlich abgeben" in the browser dialog (Playwright: handle `page.on("dialog")`).

Session expiry loses unsaved entries, so compute everything first and fill the form in one go. Going back clears
later steps.

## 8. Fair-play red lines (a reject means no run at all)

- Any value from the public scenario in code, prompts, notes, tests or defaults: tender reference, company, VAT id,
  material numbers, prices, discounts, totals, logins, TANs. Read them from the brief and the sites at run time.
- A fixed click path, a crawler that dumps the sites into one model call, or a model used only as a fallback.
- Calling any host other than the platform and the 4 sites, any model outside the proxy, a local model, or your own
  browser.
- API keys in the package (use team secrets).
- Text that tries to steer the AI reviewer counts against you. A plain README explaining the design is fine.
- Test fixtures must use clearly fake numbers so the reviewer never mistakes them for copied values.

## 9. Iteration loop

```sh
atira models proxy                         # terminal 1, keep open
eval "$(atira scout --env)"                # terminal 2
uv run --no-sync python agent.py           # local run against the public sites (nothing counts)
python ../notes/diff.py out.json           # your own diff against the hand answer (keep outside agent/)
atira test-run . --follow                  # sandbox run with the per-field score breakdown
atira submit .                             # review, then one scored run on the public board
atira status
```

- Up to 4 test runs at a time per team, 3 more can wait. Use them in parallel to measure variance.
- In Claude Code with the MCP: `diagnose_run`, `run_screenshot`, `run_profile`, `compare_runs`.
- One scored submission in flight at a time. Review takes minutes, the run up to 20. Plan about 30-40 min per cycle.

## 10. Final-hour protocol

- [ ] Feature freeze about 90 min before the deadline.
- [ ] 3-4 parallel test runs of the candidate. Pick the package with the best **worst** run.
- [ ] Submit it no later than 60 min before the deadline. Wait for review passed and the score.
- [ ] If it regresses, re-submit the last good tarball (`atira package <sub_id> --out dir`) so that one is latest.
- [ ] `atira status` shows best of 3. Repo linked. Nothing submitted after the final candidate.

## 11. Demo day (if picked)

- One-line start: `atira test-run ./agent` opens the live run view (timer, model calls, cost, score).
- Download a recording of a good run as fallback (`GET /v1/runs/<id>/video`).
- The pitch in three lines: the model navigates and decides, code checks and computes, every number in the bid points
  to its source in the evidence ledger.

## 12. Still unknown

- Submission deadline and final run time: ask the organizers.
- How many private scenarios, and whether one could be a no_bid case: build for both.
- The logged-in side of the 4 sites was not scouted for this plan. Confirm the traps in section 6 during the
  hand-solve (P1).

1	# Prepare a tender response
2	
3	You work in sales engineering for Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH, a German hydraulics and components manufacturer. Prepare one net EUR bid for Stadt Buchenstadt, Verkehrsbetriebe: Lieferung von Hydraulikzylinder für Werkstatt-Hebeanlagen (VG-2027-7093). The scenario date is 2027-01-25T09:00:00Z; the tender deadline is 2027-02-12T11:00:00Z.
4	
5	Collect the tender and its clarifications from the tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`), the technical specification from the buyer's supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`), materials and prices from the internal ERP (`erp`), and discount approvals from the sales mailbox in the webmail (Werkpost, `mail`). The websites are in German; obsolete documents and unrelated records are present.
6	
7	## Rules
8	
9	1. Quantity: start with the original tender quantity. For each position, use the quantity in the latest dated clarification that changes that position, if any.
10	2. Requirement: use the requirement referenced by the position in the specification revision marked current. Superseded revisions do not apply.
11	3. Material: select an active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all exactly equal that requirement. Blocked materials do not qualify. If any position has no matching active material, submit no_bid.
12	4. Unit price: use the material's price condition valid on the scenario date, including both validity endpoints. Choose the scale with the highest minimum quantity no greater than the final quantity. Apply the approved discount to that scale price and round the resulting unit price half up to the nearest cent.
13	5. Discount: use the most recent message from the sales director (leitung@ followed by the bidder's mailbox domain) that approves a discount for this exact tender reference. Approvals for other references and messages from other senders do not apply. If there is no approval, use zero percent.
14	6. Lead time: use the delivery-from-stock lead time in weeks when stock covers the final quantity; otherwise use the production lead time in weeks.
15	7. Total: sum each final quantity multiplied by its rounded discounted unit price, then round the total net amount half up to the nearest cent.
16	8. Decision: submit bid with one entry per tender position, identified by its position number, and currency EUR. If any active matching material is missing, submit no_bid with no positions and a total of zero.
17	
18	
19	## Additional rules
20	
21	These refine rules 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 above. Every submitted quantity is in pieces.
22	
23	- Partial submission: full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
24	- Finding records: the specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
25	- Agent requirement: a language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
26	- Commercial clauses: a tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
27	- Withdrawn answers: a tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
28	- Scoped amendments: after selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
29	- Shared stock: sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
30	- Conditional discount: the latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
31	- Units: tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
32	- Pricing breakdown: base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
33	- These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.

# Prepare a tender response

You work in sales engineering for Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH, a German hydraulics and components manufacturer. Prepare one net EUR bid for Stadt Buchenstadt, Verkehrsbetriebe: Lieferung von Hydraulikzylinder für Werkstatt-Hebeanlagen (VG-2027-7093). 1. Quantity: start with the original tender quantity. For each position, use the quantity in the latest dated clarification that changes that position, if any.
2. Requirement: use the requirement referenced by the position in the specification revision marked current. Superseded revisions do not apply.
3. Material: select an active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all exactly equal that requirement. Blocked materials do not qualify. If any position has no matching active material, submit no_bid.
4. Unit price: use the material's price condition valid on the scenario date, including both validity endpoints. Choose the scale with the highest minimum quantity no greater than the final quantity. Apply the approved discount to that scale price and round the resulting unit price half up to the nearest cent.
5. Discount: use the most recent message from the sales director (leitung@ followed by the bidder's mailbox domain) that approves a discount for this exact tender reference. Approvals for other references and messages from other senders do not apply. If there is no approval, use zero percent.
6. Lead time: use the delivery-from-stock lead time in weeks when stock covers the final quantity; otherwise use the production lead time in weeks.
7. Total: sum each final quantity multiplied by its rounded discounted unit price, then round the total net amount half up to the nearest cent.
8. Decision: submit bid with one entry per tender position, identified by its position number, and currency EUR. If any active matching material is missing, submit no_bid with no positions and a total of zero.

Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
- Agent requirement: a language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.

- Shared setup: Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
- Project bonus: the finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.
- Final price: clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.
- Metal indices: select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.
- Scoring in bid cases: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. Within each equally weighted position: material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%. Each field is independent; optional breakdown fields can be blank. No-bid scoring is unchanged.

Collect the tender and its clarifications from the tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`), the technical specification from the buyer's supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`), materials and prices from the internal ERP (`erp`), and discount approvals from the sales mailbox in the webmail (Werkpost, `mail`). The websites are in German; obsolete documents and unrelated records are present.

## Rules

1. Quantity: start with the original tender quantity. For each position, use the quantity in the latest dated clarification that changes that position, if any.
2. Requirement: use the requirement referenced by the position in the specification revision marked current. Superseded revisions do not apply.
3. Material: select an active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all exactly equal that requirement. Blocked materials do not qualify. If any position has no matching active material, submit no_bid.
4. Unit price: use the material's price condition valid on the scenario date, including both validity endpoints. Choose the scale with the highest minimum quantity no greater than the final quantity. Apply the approved discount to that scale price and round the resulting unit price half up to the nearest cent.
5. Discount: use the most recent message from the sales director (leitung@ followed by the bidder's mailbox domain) that approves a discount for this exact tender reference. Approvals for other references and messages from other senders do not apply. If there is no approval, use zero percent.
6. Lead time: use the delivery-from-stock lead time in weeks when stock covers the final quantity; otherwise use the production lead time in weeks.
7. Total: sum each final quantity multiplied by its rounded discounted unit price, then round the total net amount half up to the nearest cent.
8. Decision: submit bid with one entry per tender position, identified by its position number, and currency EUR. If any active matching material is missing, submit no_bid with no positions and a total of zero.


## Additional rules

These refine rules 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 above. Every submitted quantity is in pieces.

- Partial submission: full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
- Finding records: the specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
- Agent requirement: a language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
- Commercial clauses: a tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
- Withdrawn answers: a tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
- Scoped amendments: after selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
- Shared stock: sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
- Conditional discount: the latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
- Units: tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
- Pricing breakdown: base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
- These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
- Technical derivation: for a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
- Authority and time: resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.
- Currency: the valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.
- Packaging: Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.
- Delivery: Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.
- Shared setup: Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
- Project bonus: the finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.
- Final price: clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.
- Metal indices: select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.
- Scoring in bid cases: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. When present, the withdrawn Q&A quantity and date-selected metal-index checks earn 5 points each. Within each equally weighted position: material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%. Each field is independent; optional breakdown fields can be blank. No-bid scoring is unchanged.

## Site access

- tender-portal: https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run
  Username: `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` · Password: `REDACTED`
- customer-portal: https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run
  Username: `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` · Password: `REDACTED`
- erp: https://atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run
  Username: `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` · Password: `REDACTED`
- mail: https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run
  Username: `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` · Password: `REDACTED`

## Submission

Submit through the tender portal's "Angebotsabgabe" at https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run, after "Teilnahme bekunden" for this tender. Register the bidder using the company name Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH and USt-IdNr. DE811234567. Choose Hauptangebot for bid or Verzichtserklärung for no_bid. Complete the material configurator, enter the discounted net unit prices and total in German number format, and acknowledge the tender documents. The displayed gross amount includes VAT and is not the required net total. Retrieve the signing TAN from the bidder's webmail, review the summary, and confirm "Angebot verbindlich abgeben" in the browser dialog.

Exactly one submission is allowed; submitting ends the run. Wall-clock time and LLM tokens count toward your result. Unsaved entries are lost when the portal session expires. Going back clears the later steps. A new TAN request invalidates the previous TAN; each TAN is valid for five minutes.

=================== README.md
# Atira starter kit

A minimal starting point, not an agent. It does the platform plumbing: it reads the run, attaches to the run's
browsers and shows how to call the free hosted models. Then it stops at `solve()` in `agent.py`, the place for your
agent. Out of the box it exits without an answer.

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `run.py` | The run contract: reads the run (`load_run`) and submits an API answer (`submit_answer`) |
| `browsers.py` | Attaches to the run's browsers over CDP and gets a page (`connect`); locally it starts a Chromium |
| `models.py` | One call to each hosted model: `ask_qwen` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) and `ask_clef` (Cloudflare Clef) |
| `agent.py` | The entry point: reads the run, connects browser 1, calls `solve(task, page)` and submits what it returns |
| `agent.json` | How the sandbox installs (`uv sync`, the versions in `uv.lock`) and runs it; it waits for the hosted `qwen` |
| `tests/` | The plumbing against fakes |

## Your agent goes in `solve()`

`solve(task, page)` gets the run and a Playwright page in browser 1:

- `task["brief"]`: the task and its rules;
- `task["access"]`: each website's `siteId`, `url` and `credentials`;
- `task["submission"]`: where the answer goes, `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` or `{"kind": "site", "url": ...}`;
- `task["answer_schema"]`: the JSON Schema of the answer.

For an `api` submission, return the answer and `main()` submits it: `202` is accepted and final, `400` lists the
issues to fix. For a `site` submission, enter the answer on that website yourself and return `None`. Reading pages,
acting on them and working out the answer are yours to build.

Mind the clock: a scored run has 20 minutes, and `run.seconds_left(task)` says how many seconds are left. Every part
of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
searching; an answer that comes too late scores 0.

More browsers: set `"browsers": 2` (up to 4) in `agent.json`, then `await browsers.connect(playwright, 1)` attaches
to browser 2.

## The hosted models in short

Both are free and need no key of yours: runs get the variables, and locally `atira scout --env` sets them, pointed
at `atira models proxy`.

```python
import models

text = await models.ask_qwen("Which button submits this form? ...")          # QWEN_BASE_URL, QWEN_API_KEY
yes = await models.ask_clef({"page": page_text}, "Is this the current revision?")  # CLEF_BASE_URL, CLEF_API_KEY
```

`models.qwen()` is an OpenAI SDK client, for tool calls, images and everything else. Clef is set only where the
platform hosts it; if your agent relies on it, list `"models": ["qwen", "clef"]` in `agent.json` so the run waits for
it to warm up. Another provider works with your own key through the run's metering proxy:
`$API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls`.

## Run it locally

You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (open a new terminal after installing it, so
it is on your PATH) and the Atira CLI, signed in once with `atira login`.

Terminal 1: start the free models and leave it open.

```sh
atira models proxy
```

Terminal 2, in this folder:

```sh
uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
eval "$(atira scout --env)"     # the scouting logins, and the model variables pointed at that proxy
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

In PowerShell on Windows, Terminal 2:

```powershell
uv sync; uv run playwright install chromium
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression    # the same exports
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

A Chromium window opens (`HEADLESS=1` hides it). Nothing done with the scouting logins counts, and locally an answer
is printed, never submitted. If `atira` says `Unknown command: models`, run `atira upgrade`.

## Test-run it, then submit it

```sh
atira test-run .   # the sandbox, exactly like a scored run, on the public dataset; opens the run page live
atira submit .     # reviewed, then run once and scored for the leaderboard
```

Both pack this directory without what `.gitignore` excludes.

## Environment

| Variable | Set by | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | runs | the run, at `/v1/runs/current` |
| `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` | `atira scout --env` | locally: the brief and the scouting logins |
| `CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS` | runs | the sandbox's browsers; locally the kit starts its own Chromium |
| `QWEN_BASE_URL`, `QWEN_API_KEY` | runs, `atira scout --env` | the hosted Qwen |
| `CLEF_BASE_URL`, `CLEF_API_KEY` | runs, `atira scout --env`, when Clef is hosted | the hosted Clef |

## Docs

- How a run works: `$API/docs/run-contract.md`
- Building an agent: `$API/docs/building-an-agent.md`
- Fair play, the rules: `$API/docs/fair-play.md`

## Tests

```sh
uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests
```
=================== agent.json
{
  "setup": ["uv", "sync"],
  "run": ["uv", "run", "--no-sync", "python", "agent.py"],
  "models": ["qwen"]
}
=================== pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "atira-rfq-starter"
version = "0.2.0"
description = "A starting point for an Atira challenge agent: the run contract, the browsers, the hosted models"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
# pinned, so the run step gets the versions the kit was tested with
dependencies = ["openai==2.54.0", "playwright==1.63.0"]

[tool.uv]
package = false
=================== run.py
"""The run contract: read the run (the brief, the websites and their logins, where the answer goes), submit the answer.

In a test run or a scored run the platform sets CHALLENGE_API_URL and CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN. On your own machine there
is no run token: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` exports the public scouting run as CHALLENGE_SCOUTING instead, and
nothing done with those logins counts. Docs: $API/docs/run-contract.md
"""
import json
import os
import time
from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

USER_AGENT = "atira-starter-kit/3"  # the API's edge refuses Python's default urllib agent
LOAD_SCOUTING = 'eval "$(atira scout --env)"; in PowerShell: atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression'


def http(url: str, token: str | None = None, payload: dict | None = None, timeout: float = 30) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """GET (or POST `payload` as JSON) with the run token in x-api-key: the status and the body."""
    headers = {"Accept": "application/json", "User-Agent": USER_AGENT}
    if token:
        headers["x-api-key"] = token
    data = None
    if payload is not None:
        data = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode()
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    try:
        with urlopen(Request(url, data=data, headers=headers), timeout=timeout) as response:
            return response.status, response.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    except HTTPError as error:
        return error.code, error.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")


def load_run(env=os.environ) -> tuple[dict, str | None]:
    """The run and its token; locally, without a token, the scouting run that `atira scout --env` exported.

    The run has `brief` (the task and its rules, markdown), `access` (per website: `siteId`, `url`, `credentials`),
    `submission` (`kind` "api" or "site", and its `url`), `answer_schema`, `started_at` and `expires_at`.
    """
    token = env.get("CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN")
    if not token:
        if not env.get("CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"):
            raise SystemExit(f"No run token and no scouting logins. To develop locally: {LOAD_SCOUTING}")
        try:
            return json.loads(env["CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"]), None
        except ValueError:
            raise SystemExit(f"CHALLENGE_SCOUTING is not the JSON atira exports. Load it again: {LOAD_SCOUTING}")
    url = env["CHALLENGE_API_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/runs/current"
    status, body = 0, ""
    for attempt in range(5):  # rides out a restart of the API
        try:
            status, body = http(url, token)
        except (URLError, OSError) as error:
            status, body = 0, str(error)
        if status == 200:
            return json.loads(body), token
        if status in (401, 403, 404):  # the run is over, or the token is wrong: no point in asking again
            break
        time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))
    raise SystemExit(f"Cannot read the run: HTTP {status} {body[:300]}")


def seconds_left(run: dict, now: float | None = None) -> float:
    """Seconds until the run's `expires_at` (epoch milliseconds); after that the answer is refused and the run scores
    0. Every part of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before time runs out
    rather than keep searching."""
    expires_at = run.get("expires_at")
    if not expires_at:
        return float("inf")
    return expires_at / 1000 - (time.time() if now is None else now)


def submit_answer(run: dict, token: str | None, answer: dict) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """POST the answer to the run's "api" submission target. 202: accepted and final, the run ends. 400: the body
    lists the issues; nothing is recorded, fix the answer and send it again. A "site" submission is entered on that
    website instead, and the website confirms it with a receipt."""
    submission = run["submission"]
    if submission.get("kind") != "api":
        raise ValueError(f"This run takes its answer on the website {submission.get('url')}, not through the API")
    if not token:
        raise ValueError("No run to answer: locally there is no run token. Test it in a run: atira test-run .")
    return http(run.get("answer_url") or submission["url"], token, answer, timeout=60)
=================== models.py
"""The free hosted models in short: one call each. Docs: $API/start#models and $API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls

Qwen (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next): an OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls, images and a 256k context. Every run gets
QWEN_BASE_URL and QWEN_API_KEY; on your machine `atira scout --env` points them at `atira models proxy`, which you
keep running in another terminal.

Clef (Cloudflare Clef): a decision model. POST $CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide with a `state`, up to 4 `images` and your
`questions`: "choice" picks one of your options, "noul" gives the probability of yes, "score" rates on your scale.
CLEF_BASE_URL and CLEF_API_KEY are set only where the platform hosts Clef. A run waits only for the models listed in
agent.json "models" to warm up: list ["qwen", "clef"] if your agent relies on Clef.

Any other provider works with your own key, through the run's metering proxy: see the docs above.
"""
import os

import httpx  # comes with the OpenAI SDK
from openai import AsyncOpenAI

QWEN_MODEL = "qwen3.8-flash-next"


def qwen() -> AsyncOpenAI:
    """A client for the hosted Qwen; a cold model takes a while to answer its first call, hence the long timeout."""
    return AsyncOpenAI(base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"], api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"], timeout=360)


async def ask_qwen(prompt: str) -> str:
    """One chat call: the reply's text."""
    reply = await qwen().chat.completions.create(model=QWEN_MODEL, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}])
    return reply.choices[0].message.content or ""


async def ask_clef(state, question: str) -> float:
    """One decision: how likely Clef finds the answer to a yes/no question about `state` (text or JSON) is yes."""
    body = {"state": state, "questions": {"q": {"type": "noul", "instructions": question}}}
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=120) as client:
        response = await client.post(os.environ["CLEF_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/decide", json=body,
                                     headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CLEF_API_KEY']}"})
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()["answers"]["q"]["noul"]
=================== browsers.py
"""The run's browsers: attach over CDP and get a page. Driving them is up to you.

In a run the sandbox starts the browsers (agent.json "browsers": 1 to 4, default 1) before the clock starts and sets
CDP_URL (browser 1) and CDP_URLS (all of them, as a JSON array). Use those: the sandbox stops browsers your agent
starts itself. On your own machine there is no CDP_URLS, so `connect` starts a local Chromium (once:
`uv run playwright install chromium`; HEADLESS=1 hides it). Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md
"""
import json
import os


def cdp_urls(env=os.environ) -> list[str]:
    """Every browser of the run, in order; [] on your own machine."""
    try:
        urls = [url for url in json.loads(env.get("CDP_URLS") or "[]") if isinstance(url, str)]
    except ValueError:
        urls = []
    return urls or ([env["CDP_URL"]] if env.get("CDP_URL") else [])


async def connect(playwright, number: int = 0):
    """Browser `number` of the run (0 is browser 1) and a page in it. Locally, a Chromium of its own."""
    urls = cdp_urls()
    if urls:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.connect_over_cdp(urls[number])
        context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else await browser.new_context()
    else:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.launch(headless=os.environ.get("HEADLESS") == "1")
        context = await browser.new_context()
    page = context.pages[0] if context.pages else await context.new_page()
    return browser, page
=================== agent.py
"""Your agent's entry point: agent.json runs `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`, in the sandbox and on your machine.

The kit only does the plumbing: run.py reads the run and submits an answer, browsers.py attaches to the run's
browsers, models.py calls the hosted Qwen and Clef. Everything else is yours to build, in `solve` below.
Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md, $API/docs/run-contract.md, and the rules: $API/docs/fair-play.md
"""
import asyncio
import json
import sys

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

import browsers
import models  # noqa: F401  models.ask_qwen, models.ask_clef: see models.py
import run as contract


async def solve(task: dict, page) -> dict | None:
    """TODO: your agent goes here.

    `task` is the run: task["brief"] (the task and its rules), task["access"] (each website's url and login),
    task["submission"] (where the answer goes) and task["answer_schema"]. `page` is a Playwright page in browser 1.

    For an "api" submission, return the answer and main() submits it. For a "site" submission, enter the answer on
    that website yourself, then return None.

    Mind the clock: a scored run has 20 minutes, and `contract.seconds_left(task)` says how many are left. Every part
    of the answer scores on its own, so stop and submit your best answer about a minute before the end; an answer
    that comes too late scores 0.
    """
    return None


async def main() -> int:
    task, token = contract.load_run()
    sites = ", ".join(f"{site.get('siteId')} {site.get('url')}" for site in task["access"])
    print(f"Run {task.get('run_id') or '(local: the scouting logins, nothing counts)'}; websites: {sites}; "
          f"answer via {task['submission']['kind']}", flush=True)
    async with async_playwright() as playwright:
        browser, page = await browsers.connect(playwright)  # more browsers: browsers.connect(playwright, 1), ...
        answer = await solve(task, page)
    if answer is None:
        print("No answer to submit: build your agent in solve() in agent.py", flush=True)
        return 0
    if not token:
        print("Your answer (locally nothing is submitted):", json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
        return 0
    status, body = contract.submit_answer(task, token, answer)
    print(f"Answer: HTTP {status} {body[:2000]}", flush=True)
    return 0 if status == 202 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))

    "submission": {"kind": "api", "url": "http://placeholder/v1/runs/current/answer"},
}


class FakeServer:
    """One HTTP server for the API and the models: answers each request with the next scripted reply per path."""

    def __init__(self, replies: dict[str, list[tuple[int, dict]]]):
        self.replies, self.requests = replies, []
        fake = self

        class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def log_message(self, *args):
                pass

            def handle_one(self):
                length = int(self.headers.get("content-length") or 0)
                body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length)) if length else None
                # self.headers matches header names in any case: urllib sends X-api-key
                fake.requests.append({"method": self.command, "path": self.path, "headers": self.headers,
                                      "body": body})
                status, reply = fake.replies[self.path].pop(0)
                data = json.dumps(reply).encode()
                self.send_response(status)
                self.send_header("content-type", "application/json")
                self.send_header("content-length", str(len(data)))
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(data)

            do_GET = do_POST = handle_one

        self.server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        self.url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_address[1]}"
        threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()

    def close(self):
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()

=================== README.md
# Atira starter kit

A minimal starting point, not an agent. It does the platform plumbing: it reads the run, attaches to the run's
browsers and shows how to call the free hosted models. Then it stops at `solve()` in `agent.py`, the place for your
agent. Out of the box it exits without an answer.

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `run.py` | The run contract: reads the run (`load_run`) and submits an API answer (`submit_answer`) |
| `browsers.py` | Attaches to the run's browsers over CDP and gets a page (`connect`); locally it starts a Chromium |
| `models.py` | One call to each hosted model: `ask_qwen` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) and `ask_clef` (Cloudflare Clef) |
| `agent.py` | The entry point: reads the run, connects browser 1, calls `solve(task, page)` and submits what it returns |
| `agent.json` | How the sandbox installs (`uv sync`, the versions in `uv.lock`) and runs it; it waits for the hosted `qwen` |
| `tests/` | The plumbing against fakes |

## Your agent goes in `solve()`

`solve(task, page)` gets the run and a Playwright page in browser 1:

- `task["brief"]`: the task and its rules;
- `task["access"]`: each website's `siteId`, `url` and `credentials`;
- `task["submission"]`: where the answer goes, `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` or `{"kind": "site", "url": ...}`;
- `task["answer_schema"]`: the JSON Schema of the answer.

For an `api` submission, return the answer and `main()` submits it: `202` is accepted and final, `400` lists the
issues to fix. For a `site` submission, enter the answer on that website yourself and return `None`. Reading pages,
acting on them and working out the answer are yours to build.

Mind the clock: a scored run has 20 minutes, and `run.seconds_left(task)` says how many seconds are left. Every part
of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
searching; an answer that comes too late scores 0.

More browsers: set `"browsers": 2` (up to 4) in `agent.json`, then `await browsers.connect(playwright, 1)` attaches
to browser 2.

## The hosted models in short

Both are free and need no key of yours: runs get the variables, and locally `atira scout --env` sets them, pointed
at `atira models proxy`.

```python
import models

text = await models.ask_qwen("Which button submits this form? ...")          # QWEN_BASE_URL, QWEN_API_KEY
yes = await models.ask_clef({"page": page_text}, "Is this the current revision?")  # CLEF_BASE_URL, CLEF_API_KEY
```

`models.qwen()` is an OpenAI SDK client, for tool calls, images and everything else. Clef is set only where the
platform hosts it; if your agent relies on it, list `"models": ["qwen", "clef"]` in `agent.json` so the run waits for
it to warm up. Another provider works with your own key through the run's metering proxy:
`$API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls`.

## Run it locally

You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (open a new terminal after installing it, so
it is on your PATH) and the Atira CLI, signed in once with `atira login`.

Terminal 1: start the free models and leave it open.

```sh
atira models proxy
```

Terminal 2, in this folder:

```sh
uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
eval "$(atira scout --env)"     # the scouting logins, and the model variables pointed at that proxy
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

In PowerShell on Windows, Terminal 2:

```powershell
uv sync; uv run playwright install chromium
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression    # the same exports
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

A Chromium window opens (`HEADLESS=1` hides it). Nothing done with the scouting logins counts, and locally an answer
is printed, never submitted. If `atira` says `Unknown command: models`, run `atira upgrade`.

## Test-run it, then submit it

```sh
atira test-run .   # the sandbox, exactly like a scored run, on the public dataset; opens the run page live
atira submit .     # reviewed, then run once and scored for the leaderboard
```

Both pack this directory without what `.gitignore` excludes.

## Environment

| Variable | Set by | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | runs | the run, at `/v1/runs/current` |
| `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` | `atira scout --env` | locally: the brief and the scouting logins |
| `CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS` | runs | the sandbox's browsers; locally the kit starts its own Chromium |
| `QWEN_BASE_URL`, `QWEN_API_KEY` | runs, `atira scout --env` | the hosted Qwen |
| `CLEF_BASE_URL`, `CLEF_API_KEY` | runs, `atira scout --env`, when Clef is hosted | the hosted Clef |

## Docs

- How a run works: `$API/docs/run-contract.md`
- Building an agent: `$API/docs/building-an-agent.md`
- Fair play, the rules: `$API/docs/fair-play.md`

## Tests

```sh
uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests
```

"""The run contract: read the run (the brief, the websites and their logins, where the answer goes), submit the answer.

In a test run or a scored run the platform sets CHALLENGE_API_URL and CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN. On your own machine there
is no run token: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` exports the public scouting run as CHALLENGE_SCOUTING instead, and
nothing done with those logins counts. Docs: $API/docs/run-contract.md
"""
import json
import os
import time
from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

USER_AGENT = "atira-starter-kit/3"  # the API's edge refuses Python's default urllib agent
LOAD_SCOUTING = 'eval "$(atira scout --env)"; in PowerShell: atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression'


def http(url: str, token: str | None = None, payload: dict | None = None, timeout: float = 30) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """GET (or POST `payload` as JSON) with the run token in x-api-key: the status and the body."""
    headers = {"Accept": "application/json", "User-Agent": USER_AGENT}
    if token:
        headers["x-api-key"] = token
    data = None
    if payload is not None:
        data = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode()
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    try:
        with urlopen(Request(url, data=data, headers=headers), timeout=timeout) as response:
            return response.status, response.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    except HTTPError as error:
        return error.code, error.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")


def load_run(env=os.environ) -> tuple[dict, str | None]:
    """The run and its token; locally, without a token, the scouting run that `atira scout --env` exported.

    The run has `brief` (the task and its rules, markdown), `access` (per website: `siteId`, `url`, `credentials`),
    `submission` (`kind` "api" or "site", and its `url`), `answer_schema`, `started_at` and `expires_at`.
    """
    token = env.get("CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN")
    if not token:
        if not env.get("CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"):
            raise SystemExit(f"No run token and no scouting logins. To develop locally: {LOAD_SCOUTING}")
        try:
            return json.loads(env["CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"]), None
        except ValueError:
            raise SystemExit(f"CHALLENGE_SCOUTING is not the JSON atira exports. Load it again: {LOAD_SCOUTING}")
    url = env["CHALLENGE_API_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/runs/current"
    status, body = 0, ""
    for attempt in range(5):  # rides out a restart of the API
        try:
            status, body = http(url, token)
        except (URLError, OSError) as error:
            status, body = 0, str(error)
        if status == 200:
            return json.loads(body), token
        if status in (401, 403, 404):  # the run is over, or the token is wrong: no point in asking again
            break
        time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))
    raise SystemExit(f"Cannot read the run: HTTP {status} {body[:300]}")


def seconds_left(run: dict, now: float | None = None) -> float:
    """Seconds until the run's `expires_at` (epoch milliseconds); after that the answer is refused and the run scores
    0. Every part of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before time runs out
    rather than keep searching."""
    expires_at = run.get("expires_at")
    if not expires_at:
        return float("inf")
    return expires_at / 1000 - (time.time() if now is None else now)


def submit_answer(run: dict, token: str | None, answer: dict) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """POST the answer to the run's "api" submission target. 202: accepted and final, the run ends. 400: the body
    lists the issues; nothing is recorded, fix the answer and send it again. A "site" submission is entered on that
    website instead, and the website confirms it with a receipt."""
    submission = run["submission"]
    if submission.get("kind") != "api":
        raise ValueError(f"This run takes its answer on the website {submission.get('url')}, not through the API")
    if not token:
        raise ValueError("No run to answer: locally there is no run token. Test it in a run: atira test-run .")
    return http(run.get("answer_url") or submission["url"], token, answer, timeout=60)
=================== models.py
"""The free hosted models in short: one call each. Docs: $API/start#models and $API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls

Qwen (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next): an OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls, images and a 256k context. Every run gets
QWEN_BASE_URL and QWEN_API_KEY; on your machine `atira scout --env` points them at `atira models proxy`, which you
keep running in another terminal.

Clef (Cloudflare Clef): a decision model. POST $CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide with a `state`, up to 4 `images` and your
`questions`: "choice" picks one of your options, "noul" gives the probability of yes, "score" rates on your scale.
CLEF_BASE_URL and CLEF_API_KEY are set only where the platform hosts Clef. A run waits only for the models listed in
agent.json "models" to warm up: list ["qwen", "clef"] if your agent relies on Clef.

Any other provider works with your own key, through the run's metering proxy: see the docs above.
"""
import os

import httpx  # comes with the OpenAI SDK
from openai import AsyncOpenAI

QWEN_MODEL = "qwen3.8-flash-next"


def qwen() -> AsyncOpenAI:
    """A client for the hosted Qwen; a cold model takes a while to answer its first call, hence the long timeout."""
    return AsyncOpenAI(base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"], api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"], timeout=360)


async def ask_qwen(prompt: str) -> str:
    """One chat call: the reply's text."""
    reply = await qwen().chat.completions.create(model=QWEN_MODEL, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}])
    return reply.choices[0].message.content or ""


async def ask_clef(state, question: str) -> float:
    """One decision: how likely Clef finds the answer to a yes/no question about `state` (text or JSON) is yes."""
    body = {"state": state, "questions": {"q": {"type": "noul", "instructions": question}}}
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=120) as client:
        response = await client.post(os.environ["CLEF_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/decide", json=body,
                                     headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CLEF_API_KEY']}"})
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()["answers"]["q"]["noul"]
=================== browsers.py
"""The run's browsers: attach over CDP and get a page. Driving them is up to you.

In a run the sandbox starts the browsers (agent.json "browsers": 1 to 4, default 1) before the clock starts and sets
CDP_URL (browser 1) and CDP_URLS (all of them, as a JSON array). Use those: the sandbox stops browsers your agent
starts itself. On your own machine there is no CDP_URLS, so `connect` starts a local Chromium (once:
`uv run playwright install chromium`; HEADLESS=1 hides it). Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md
"""
import json
import os


def cdp_urls(env=os.environ) -> list[str]:
    """Every browser of the run, in order; [] on your own machine."""
    try:
        urls = [url for url in json.loads(env.get("CDP_URLS") or "[]") if isinstance(url, str)]
    except ValueError:
        urls = []
    return urls or ([env["CDP_URL"]] if env.get("CDP_URL") else [])


async def connect(playwright, number: int = 0):
    """Browser `number` of the run (0 is browser 1) and a page in it. Locally, a Chromium of its own."""
    urls = cdp_urls()
    if urls:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.connect_over_cdp(urls[number])
        context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else await browser.new_context()
    else:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.launch(headless=os.environ.get("HEADLESS") == "1")
        context = await browser.new_context()
    page = context.pages[0] if context.pages else await context.new_page()
    return browser, page
=================== agent.py
"""Your agent's entry point: agent.json runs `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`, in the sandbox and on your machine.

The kit only does the plumbing: run.py reads the run and submits an answer, browsers.py attaches to the run's
browsers, models.py calls the hosted Qwen and Clef. Everything else is yours to build, in `solve` below.
Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md, $API/docs/run-contract.md, and the rules: $API/docs/fair-play.md
"""
import asyncio
import json
import sys

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

import browsers
import models  # noqa: F401  models.ask_qwen, models.ask_clef: see models.py

    "access": [{"siteId": "tender-portal", "url": "https://tender.example/",

    "submission": {"kind": "api", "url": "http://placeholder/v1/runs/current/answer"},
}


class FakeServer:
    """One HTTP server for the API and the models: answers each request with the next scripted reply per path."""

    def __init__(self, replies: dict[str, list[tuple[int, dict]]]):
        self.replies, self.requests = replies, []
        fake = self

        class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def log_message(self, *args):
                pass

            def handle_one(self):
                length = int(self.headers.get("content-length") or 0)
                body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length)) if length else None
                # self.headers matches header names in any case: urllib sends X-api-key
                fake.requests.append({"method": self.command, "path": self.path, "headers": self.headers,
                                      "body": body})
                status, reply = fake.replies[self.path].pop(0)
                data = json.dumps(reply).encode()
                self.send_response(status)
                self.send_header("content-type", "application/json")
                self.send_header("content-length", str(len(data)))
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(data)

            do_GET = do_POST = handle_one

        self.server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        self.url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_address[1]}"
        threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()

    def close(self):
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()


class Case(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    def serve(self, replies):
        server = FakeServer(replies)
        self.addCleanup(server.close)
